_format: Newest day first. Each day: { date: YYYY-MM-DD, entries: [ { type: feature | improvement | fix | internal, text, refs?: [ '#12', 'PR #1', 'commit abc1234' ] } ] }. Refs become new-tab GitHub links. Update this file in the same commit as every user-visible change (see AGENTS.md).

entries.text: The settings menu is shorter: it now opens on a short list of sections (Look, Sound, Streaming, Developer, Feedback) that each say what they are set to, and one tap opens the one you want.
Streaming: a new preference "Keep my IP always private" sends every connection through the relay server, so nobody in the room learns your IP address.
Spectators only watch: they can no longer change the game or the settings, start, ask for a rematch or send everyone back to the room. Chat and reactions still work.
The number of players is picked right in the lobby (2 / 3 / 4) instead of inside the settings; games that don't take that many players are grayed out.
Online: a player or spectator whose first connection attempt stalled and who reconnected no longer counts twice in the room.
Bot levels are fully deterministic: each level searches a fixed number of positions per move, the same on every device, instead of a time limit.

Preferences: the slider and the sound set line up with the checkboxes, the sections are separated, hints are left-aligned; the bot dialog lost its rating boilerplate; fewer entries in the default changelog view.
Changelog: by default only what changes the game for you is listed; a toggle shows the technical entries too.
Hide the room code for streaming: the eye button next to the code hides it in the lobby, the game and the address bar (share and copy keep working); the preferences can hide it by default.
One bot per game, simply called Bot: the opponent dialog is a single step with the difficulty; the Random bots are no longer offered.
Preferences: the Look control is full width, the rows have more room, the dialog is wider on desktop, and the corner button says Settings & Feedback.
Settings: the rows are evenly spaced again.
No more em dashes in the texts.
Changelog entries are more compact: type and links on one line, the text below.
Big refactor: the games plug into a generic framework (HUD, settings rows, win chance, replay-ready game records); the app is split into table, room and screens. Nothing changes for players.
Changelog button on the title screen (this list).
The textured looks are now called "Blocks board" and "Blocks".
Add to home screen on Android: the page installs like an app, with a new icon.

Win chance is much calmer: it no longer changes during explosion animations, both bots evaluate positions properly (no more turn-to-turn flip-flops), the numbers are calibrated on real games, refined in the background while nobody moves, and lightly smoothed between moves except when a side is clearly winning.
Five Wins ends in a draw as soon as no line can be completed any more, even with empty cells left.
The room lobby is more compact: chat lives only in the game, the share buttons sit in one row under the code.
A lone emoji floats slowly; only spam falls fast.
Five Wins defaults to an 11 × 11 board.
Bots react like players: a wave at the start, GG at the end, EZ when they see the win coming, praise for strong moves, teasing faces for blunders. Seven new emojis for everyone.
Bot picker rebuilt in two steps with both scores; picking a game no longer opens it, the default is the best bot on Normal.
Feedback button in the preferences opens a prefilled GitHub issue.
Title screen: wider on desktop, shorter button names; the Look control lives only in the preferences.
On phones the preferences button could not be tapped during a game; the reaction toggle is aligned with it; no more accidental text selection.
Spectators: when a room is full, further people watch; a spectate link can be shared.
Rooms with three or four players.
Room chat in the game log.
Sounds: placing, explosions, win/lose, your turn, reactions: synthesized for Classic, block sounds for the Blocks looks; volume and categories in the preferences.
Preferences button (⚙) on every screen: look, sound volume and categories.
Real bots: Creeper (Chain React) and Sensei (Five Wins), Easy to Very hard, rated against Random and on proven puzzle sets; the ratings show in the picker.
Live win chance for both players in every mode.
Play against a bot: bot picker with difficulty, Random bots for both games.

Online play is robust against refreshes, leaving and rejoining, a host who disappears (the other player takes over the room), a third person joining, lost rematch requests and diverged boards (automatic re-sync).
Mobile-to-mobile online play works through a relay server.
Big refactor: pure game rules, shared engine, game registry, event bus, CSS per area: no visible change.
Extensive unit and end-to-end test suite; deploys only after a green run.
Favicons and app icons deploy correctly.
Result dialog wider on desktop; the last-move marker hides after the game and no longer pulses in Five Wins.
Textures preload on the first visit with a progress bar.
Hashed bundle and automatic deploy to minigames.alzlper.com.

Chain React and Five Wins with a persistent room (one link for the whole evening), online play over PeerJS, local play, chess clock, settings shared live in the room, three looks, emoji reactions, result dialog with a look-at-board mode.
